title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measured the effect of a deterministic validator and a bounded single-repair step applied to the same sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics) in a guarded NetOps pipeline. The preregistered study targeted retrieval-augmentation (RAG) poisoning attacks, but the executed adapter contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); consequently the realized estimand compares baseline single-shot validator outcomes on a shared sampled candidate against final guarded outcomes (validator ± permitted repair) on that same candidate. On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 judged every sampled initial candidate valid (n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run; we reconcile the archived artifacts, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limitations with artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered experiments.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks (intent→configuration translation, staged maintenance workflows, zero-touch configuration) but unconstrained generations can violate operational invariants (ordering, reachability, policy). Tool‑augmented defensive architectures pair generation with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. Prior surveys and applied papers document both the promise of LLM-driven automation and the persistence of hallucination and translation errors that threaten operational correctness [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4402742293, https://openalex.org/W4403635865]. 

We preregistered study candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to quantify whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates and whether deterministic defenses mitigate that effect. The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design (N = 250 tasks), a primary poison fraction of 0.30, and a single primary estimand: the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded minus baseline) under shared task instances. During execution the adapter contract used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (artifact-backed); this executed semantics produces a different realized estimand and therefore requires careful reconciliation. 

Research question (executed estimand): When baseline and guarded arms begin from the same single sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate), does adding a deterministic validator plus at-most-one repair change the paired actionable-misconfiguration outcome for synthetic intent→configuration tasks? Our principal contribution is an artifact-grounded report of the realized paired experiment, an explicit reconciliation of preregistered aims with executed contract semantics, and evidence-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered runs that exercise the original RAG-poisoning estimand.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and application papers from 2024–2026 document rapid adoption of LLMs for NetOps problems (intent decomposition, configuration generation, zero-touch automation) while repeatedly recommending deterministic validators and tool augmentation to mitigate factual and constraint violations [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4402742293, https://openalex.org/W4403635865]. Benchmarks and frameworks (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) provide task banks and evaluation primitives but expose construct-validity concerns for operational invariants such as reachability and policy compliance [https://openalex.org/W4399629579].

Adjacent-domain work on RAG pipelines and adversarial poisoning (security operations, code translation) documents concrete failure modes—hallucination, adversarially induced misinformation, and translation bugs—that motivate controlled adversarial evaluations for NetOps RAG pipelines [10.20944/preprints202512.0913.v1]. Tool-augmented proposals (LLMs calling deterministic verifiers/simulators) show promise for grounding but entail tradeoffs in latency and engineering complexity [https://openalex.org/W4389518608, doi:10.2139/ssrn.7317098]. Importantly, the supplied literature set contains proposals and controlled demonstrations but lacks a broad, topology-grounded empirical measurement of RAG-poisoning effects on operational invariants; this gap motivated our preregistration.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration summary. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 with primary hypothesis H1 (poisoned retrieval fragments at poison_fraction = 0.30 increase actionable misconfigurations) and a secondary mitigation hypothesis H2 (deterministic retrieval filters reduce but do not eliminate poisoning effects). The preregistration artifact is archived; its SHA‑256 is ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3 (referenced in the execution manifest). The preregistration defined a paired confirmatory design with N_confirmatory = 250 tasks and a complete_pair_primary exclusion rule (pairs with missing condition outputs are excluded). Power was calibrated assuming baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05 to detect an absolute paired increase ≈ 0.045–0.06 at 80% power.

Executed adapter contract and critical runtime fields (artifact-backed). The adapter family executed was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with declared_model_version gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Key executed contract fields (archived): generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded arms); retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals performed); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; task_count = 250; planned_episode_count = 500; completed_episode_count = 500; model_calls_used = 250. The model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0. We emphasize this explicit statement because unset temperature does not guarantee deterministic sampling for hosted models.

Sampling semantics and comparison logic. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics each task produced exactly one sampled candidate (shared_initial_generation stage); that same text was evaluated under both conditions. Baseline = validator outcome on the shared sampled candidate. Guarded = final outcome after the deterministic validator and at‑most‑one permitted repair invoked only when the validator indicated a violation. The paired binary outcome per task is actionable_misconfig ∈ {0,1} defined as 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION where VALID_CONFIGURATION is the validator's binary judgment archived per episode. Because baseline and guarded began from the identical sampled candidate, any paired difference could only arise from the validator-triggered repair step.

Reconciliation and recorded deviation. The preregistration targeted RAG/poisoning; the executed contract disabled retrievals, so the original RAG hypothesis was not testable. The archival facts are explicit: execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 a40e96e2...) records retrieval_augmented_generation = false; execution manifest records model_calls_used = 250 and stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 250}. The archived analysis_results metadata contains deviations_from_preregistration = [] (no post-hoc deviation entry). To reconcile these items we add an explicit Deviations statement in this Methods section referencing the two artifacts above: the run adhered to the frozen executed contract archived in execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json; that contract disabled retrievals, therefore the RAG poisoning hypotheses were not executed. This manuscript documents that execution-time realization and points readers to the archived artifacts (see model_configuration.json sha256 a40e96e2... and preregistration sha ebfbe67f5...).

Data, validators, and scoring. Task bank: synthetic intent→configuration tasks generated deterministically (task_count = 250; representative task entries and reference answers archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl; example pair task-000004 reference answer sha256 c8b7cf48...). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 produced per-episode VALID_CONFIGURATION judgments and validator_traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json (representative artifact hashes recorded in the execution manifest). Repair policy: at most one repair call per failing candidate; repair traces are null for all episodes because no repairs were applied. All raw outputs and traces are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256 e3af400a9...).

Statistical analysis. Primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided test for paired binary outcomes (α = 0.05) with paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Missingness handling: preregistered complete_pair_primary (exclude any pair with missing condition); the run produced zero exclusions. All analysis CSVs and logs are archived under analysis/ with hashes in the manifest.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run started 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z (execution manifest). Planned episodes 500 (two conditions × 250 tasks) completed with failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 250; cache_miss_count = 250; stage_counts show one shared_initial_generation stage executed 250 times (no independent per-condition sampling). Model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 a40e96e212ab87da...). Raw results and response files are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256 e3af400a9...).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256 1be58d82...) records n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0; guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0. Under actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION this yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms and paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv (hashes recorded) confirm no missingness or exclusions.

Representative artifacts and repair traces. Representative episode artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json, task-000004-guarded.json, etc.; representative raw-response sha256 2d39d60d...) show identical shared_initial_candidate content across baseline and guarded arms and validator traces with validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false. No repair_provider_trace entries appear in the archive because the guard never invoked repairs. The deterministic_reconciliation.json (analysis artifact) records provider_call_audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 250 and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false, consistent with a single shared generation per task.

Power and assumption mismatch. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05; the observed baseline = 0.0 violates that assumption. Consequently, the run lacks sensitivity to detect the originally preregistered RAG-poisoning effect sizes. We report this power/assumption mismatch explicitly and archive the artifacts supporting this conclusion (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256 1be58d82..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl sha f36cac00...).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation constrained to executed estimand. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the deterministic validator used, every sampled candidate satisfied validator checks for the synthetic task bank; thus the guarded pipeline (validator ± allowed repair) could not alter paired outcomes and the paired difference is zero. This result is an artifact-grounded demonstration of the null effect of a validator/repair when initial candidates are already valid and repairs are not triggered.

What the results do not establish. These outcomes do not imply that guarded pipelines are unnecessary. The run did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation (retrieval_augmented_generation = false), did not permit independent per-condition sampling, used a single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on synthetic tasks; therefore the run cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses nor generalize to production deployments, vendor-specific semantics, or diverse sampling regimes.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: provider and reconciliations artifacts (deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution manifest) confirm shared_initial_candidate semantics and one shared generation per task; this isolates validator/repair effects but precludes detecting effects that require per-condition sampling variability. Construct validity: the deterministic validator enforces a specific rule set and reports final_state and violation_codes in traces, but may not capture vendor-specific behaviors or asynchronous device state; validator completeness is a construct-validity limitation. External validity: synthetic task bank, single model, and single validator limit transferability to heterogeneous production topologies and multi-model ensembles. Conclusion validity: homogeneous all-success outcomes yield exact CI bounds that reflect the controlled corpus rather than operational heterogeneity; the original power assumptions do not hold in this execution.

Reconciliation of archived metadata and reviewer concern. A reviewer noted that archived analysis_results metadata contained deviations_from_preregistration = [] while the run did not exercise RAG. We reconcile these facts: the run followed the frozen executed adapter contract archived in execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 a40e96e2...) which explicitly set retrieval_augmented_generation = false; the preregistration artifact (sha256 ebfbe67f5...) documents the conceptual RAG plan. Because the executed contract differed from the conceptual RAG plan, the run adhered to the executed contract and produced results under those semantics; we document this execution-time realization here and reference the concrete artifacts demonstrating the contract state.

Operational implications and next-step preregistration. To test the original RAG-poisoning estimand requires (1) enabling retrieval_augmented_generation and deterministic poison injection at controlled poison_fraction levels, (2) permitting independent per-condition generation (generation_semantics != shared_initial_candidate), (3) constructing a provenance-flagged synthetic-poison corpus with containment checks, (4) broadening validators to vendor-aware simulators, and (5) optionally testing multiple LLM sampling regimes. We preserve these concrete, artifact-grounded recommendations as follow-up preregistration targets rather than retrofitting present evidence.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (declared model: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). All 250 shared sampled candidates passed deterministic validation (n11 = 250), no repairs were applied, and the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable; we documented and reconciled this execution-time realization against the archived preregistration and execution artifacts. Follow-up preregistered runs that enable controlled retrieval augmentation, independent per-condition sampling, broader validators, and multi-model ensembles are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

The human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Executed adapter and model: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter requesting declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses) as archived in execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json). Preregistration manifest archived under study id candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3 as referenced in the execution manifest). The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The executed adapter contract (artifact-backed) set generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across baseline and guarded arms) and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals, hence no RAG/poisoning injection). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0. All raw outputs, validator traces, analysis scripts, paired contingency artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived and referenced by the submission (see execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256 e3af400a9167c27f2255003a02cf86f7b75381f96c64697014b55b77e753514b and analysis artifacts with hashes in the execution manifest).
limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as an execution-time realization documented in the execution manifest and model_configuration.json artifact (sha256: a40e96e2...).

The stored scorer semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
